title: Google’s Data Agent Kit Hits GA, Splitting Agent Guardrails Between Skills and IAM
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Google has made Data Agent Kit generally available, a free set of MCP tools and 37 open-source skills that connect coding agents to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services. Two kinds of guardrail ship with it, and practitioners need to tell them apart: one is a skill asking the agent to stop, the other an IAM deny policy that refuses the call.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Cloudflare Reclaims 100 TB of RAM by Optimizing Consistent Hashing
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-hashing-optimization/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790410589563.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently documented how it reduced the memory footprint of its internal load-balancing service by more than 100 TB by optimizing the Rust implementation of consistent hashing in pingora-ketama. The changes compacted hash-ring entries and used statistical analysis of hash distribution and collision rates to reduce the number of hashes per backend by about 90%.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Cloudflare Brings On-Demand CPU and Memory Profiling to Production Workers
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-cpu-memory-profiling/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791971960113.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has introduced on-demand CPU and memory profiling for Workers and Durable Objects, allowing developers to investigate performance bottlenecks in production using interactive flamegraphs.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Article: Multi-Cloud FinOps: An Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/multi-cloud-finops-cost-optimization/en/headerimage/multi-cloud-finops-cost-optimization-header-1792499448017.jpg"/><p>Multi-cloud flexibility comes with hidden egress costs driven by service placement and communication patterns. This article applies Backend FinOps to cross-cloud architecture, covering cost visibility through FOCUS, workload placement, synchronization models, and CI/CD-integrated cost governance. A controlled experiment shows architecture changes saved far more than rate negotiation alone.</p> <i>By Vivek Arora</i>

title: Presentation: Move Fast, Don’t Break Trust: Shipping Constantly with Humans and Beyond
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/monzo-microservices-devex/en/mediumimage/suhail-patel-medium-1791448951499.jpg"/><p>Suhail Patel discusses how Monzo structures its software engineering organization and technical stack to ship safely hundreds of times a day. He shares insights into opinionated microservice abstractions, tenancy-based staging, static analysis checks, continuous profiling, demonstrating how a strong internal platform enables engineers and LLMs to iterate rapidly without sacrificing reliability.</p> <i>By Suhail Patel</i>

title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-agents-harbor-docker/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792589629439.jpg"/><p>Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Developer behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready"
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>A developer used Claude Opus 5.5 to build open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications, promoted them across Reddit with a projection of roughly 100% parity within a month, then told Hacker News the project was not anywhere close to ready. Its own roadmap puts it at 45% ready for real work and 2,300 to 4,100 agent-hours from full parity.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/emudhra-ca-compromise/en/headerimage/weak-link-1792602361259.jpeg"/><p>Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any site. The keys were revealed due to low entropy, not through a known breach. Browsers blocked them using revocation lists, but other software had to remove the emSign ECC G3 root. Unpatched systems remain exposed to forged certificates, including client auth and mTLS.</p> <i>By Chris Swan</i>

title: Netflix Bridges AWS IAM and Internal Identity with Workload Attestation
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Netflix has developed a workload attestation mechanism for Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR. The design combines AWS IAM identity with signed claims from Netflix’s control plane before issuing short-lived internal X.509 certificates, allowing managed compute workloads to authenticate to internal services without directly injecting credentials.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Presentation: AI is an Amplifier: Scale High Performance, Not Dysfunction
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/dora-ai-adoption-engineering-performance/en/mediumimage/medium-1791447741420.jpg"/><p>Nathen Harvey shares insights from DORA research on AI adoption in software delivery. He explains why AI acts as an amplifier, how the DORA AI Capabilities Model drives outcomes, and why engineering leaders must evolve beyond bottlenecks like code reviews to achieve sustainable productivity, reduce delivery instability, and empower developers without burning out their teams.</p> <i>By Nathen Harvey</i>

title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cilium-120-kubernetes-networking/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792161419866.jpg"/><p>Cilium 1.20 has been released with broader Kubernetes Gateway API support, an extensible eBPF datapath and further work on sidecarless mutual TLS. The release also makes the newer netkit network device easier to introduce across Kubernetes fleets that run different Linux kernel versions.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 Targets Reliability at Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/github-runner-controller-0-15/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791971221854.jpg"/><p>GitHub has released Actions Runner Controller (ARC) 0.15.0, introducing reliability, scalability, and observability improvements for organisations running self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on Kubernetes.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Buildkite Adds Scoped Secrets and New Agentic CI Tools
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/buildkite-ci-secrets-agentic/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792160661689.jpg"/><p>Continuous integration provider Buildkite has introduced pipeline-scoped secrets and new Model Context Protocol tools for validating pipelines, diagnosing failed builds and repairing webhooks. The company has also added Linux arm64 support to its GitHub Actions compatibility layer and expanded OpenTelemetry data in Buildkite Agent v4.1.0.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: AWS Introduces Preview of Well-Architected Agent
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-well-architected-agent/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791124477134.jpg"/><p>AWS recently announced the preview of the Well-Architected Agent, a service that analyzes environments against Well-Architected best practices and provides prioritized recommendations across cost, security, performance, and reliability. The AI agent can also suggest remediation steps and review infrastructure-as-code before deployment.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: AWS Will Run Its European Sovereign Cloud Without the Global Backbone for Several Hours
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-sovereign-cloud-exercise/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791945895599.jpg"/><p>On October 24, AWS will operate its European Sovereign Cloud without a connection to the AWS Global Network backbone, with a team of EU residents and the region’s own hardware and software. AWS says neither of the two systems being severed is operation-critical, and practitioners are divided over whether the exercise answers the question customers are asking.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>
